problem: Existing VLN agents follow a Seq2Seq design. They compress past observations into the latent state of recurrent units, so they cannot precisely recall past percepts or model the environment layout. They also decide only within the local action space of the currently visible navigable viewpoints, which makes earlier wrong decisions hard to correct.
motivation: Robotics has long used explicit maps (SLAM, topological maps) for planning. External-memory networks also preserve long-term information better than RNN states, which are unstable over long timescales. The authors observe that an agent keeping an explicit graph of everything it has seen could reason over the whole explored area. Such an agent could then 'jump' back to any previously observed but unvisited location, giving robust error correction.
key_idea: The agent builds an online graph-structured external memory (SSM) whose nodes hold panoramic visual features and whose directed edges hold orientation features. Perception- and action-aware instruction attention reads the nodes and edges respectively, GRU message passing reasons over the graph, and decisions are made over the global action space of all unvisited navigable viewpoints via a two-step frontier-then-sub-node policy.
insight: An explicit topological memory with a global action space mainly buys error recovery. In the R2R val-unseen ablation, restricting the full model to the local action space drops SR from 0.62 to 0.54. The same restriction shortens TL from 20.7 to 12.6 and actually raises SPL from 0.45 to 0.49, so the gains come from exploration and backtracking at the cost of path efficiency. A naive one-step policy over the ever-growing global action space trains poorly (SR 0.56, SPL 0.41), and factorizing it into frontier selection followed by sub-node selection recovers the gains. Separating visual cues (nodes) from geometric cues (edges) and grounding perception vs. action words onto each is also useful: without it val-unseen SR falls to 0.59. Removing GRU message passing drops it to 0.57.
method: SSM graph construction: an online directed graph G_t; each visited node stores the ResNet-152 features of its 36-view panorama (visual), and each directed edge e_{u,v} stores the 4-d heading/elevation (cos/sin) orientation from u toward v (geometric), so visual and geometric cues are disentangled. After a place is visited, duplicate sub-nodes pointing to it are merged into one new node.

Global action space: each node is split into K_v sub-nodes, the navigable, observed but unvisited viewpoints, and all sub-nodes in the graph form the action space. This lets the agent move to any unvisited viewpoint observed earlier; the move is executed along the shortest path over G_t.

Perception-and-action aware grounding (collect-read controller): two instruction attentions conditioned on the LSTM state h_t yield perception text x^p and action text x^a, giving states h^p and h^a. Each node attends over its panoramic visual features with h^p and over its outgoing edge orientations with h^a, following OAAM.

Iterative reasoning: S rounds of parametric message passing over the graph (sum of neighbor features, with GRU update functions), run separately for the visual and orientation streams, capture S-hop context for long-range planning.

Frontier-exploration decision making: first select a frontier node (a node with unvisited navigable sub-nodes) using a softmax over visual/orientation scores with an adaptive combination weight. The agent then travels there along the shortest graph path while updating its states, and picks one of that frontier's sub-nodes with the same visual+orientation scoring.

Training: builds on the EnvDrop agent and uses IL (teacher forcing plus student forcing, where the teacher action is the SSM node closest to the goal) combined with A2C-style RL. Frontier and action steps are both rewarded by the change in distance to goal, plus a success reward at the end. On R2R the agent additionally trains on back-translation augmented data.

setting.backbone: ImageNet ResNet-152 features (frozen) + LSTM instruction encoder + LSTM navigation state + GRU message-passing graph reasoner, built on the EnvDrop agent (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: R2R train (61 envs, 14,039 instructions) plus back-translation (Speaker-Follower/EnvDrop) synthetic augmented instructions for the R2R '*' model; R4R train (233,613 instructions) for R4R
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, ResNet-152 features) + heading/elevation orientation features
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints; global action space over all unvisited navigable viewpoints in the explored graph (frontier node selection, then sub-node selection, with shortest-path travel to the frontier)
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard R2R nav-graph (given navigability between viewpoints; viewpoint identity used to merge duplicate sub-nodes after a visit)

numbers_note: The paper prints SR, OR, SPL, CLS, nDTW and SDTW as fractions (e.g. 0.62); they are converted to 0-100 here (OR mapped to OSR). NE and TL are in meters. The paper does not state whether augmentation is used for R4R, and no R4R test results are reported. The ablation (Table 3) covers only R2R val-seen/val-unseen with the augmented model and is omitted from the numbers above. The full model row in Table 3 is identical to Ours*.
results: On R2R, SSM with back-translation augmentation reaches SR 0.62 / SPL 0.45 on val-unseen and SR 0.61 / SPL 0.46 on test-unseen. This beats Active Perception (0.60 SR / 0.41 SPL test), EGP (0.53 SR test) and Tactical Rewind (0.54 SR test) on SR. However, SPL stays below AuxRN, OAAM and EnvDrop (0.50-0.51 on test) because trajectories are longer (TL about 20 m). On R4R val-unseen it sets state of the art with CLS 0.53 vs 0.44 (EGP), plus SR 0.32, nDTW 0.39 and SDTW 0.19, and shows the smallest seen-unseen CLS gap (0.12).
limitations: Global backtracking makes trajectories long (TL about 20 m vs about 10 m for EnvDrop/OAAM), so SPL on R2R unseen splits trails several local-action baselines. The ablation shows that a local-action-space variant has higher SPL (0.49) than the full model (0.45).

Relies on the discrete R2R nav-graph (given connectivity, viewpoint identity for node merging, and shortest-path travel between graph nodes), so it is not directly applicable to continuous environments or real robots.

The global action space grows with episode length, which motivates the frontier factorization; the evaluation also uses only pre-extracted ResNet-152 features with no pretraining, and is limited to R2R/R4R.
